topic: what the system is, the api vs ws processes, and how it boots (env, cluster, scheduled jobs)
hint: Same bundle runs as api or ws: env.TYPE is set from the --ws argv flag, and worker.ts mounts the Express /api routers only when TYPE==='api'. src/index.ts primary process forks up to 3 cluster workers (1 in DEV_MODE), exits whole process if any worker dies, and starts the node-schedule/setInterval cleanup jobs only on the api type.

topic: how an HTTP request reaches its handler (global middleware order, per-route middleware chain, router registration)
hint: worker.ts order: helmet, cors, json, userIP, OpenGraphRouter, global_limit rateLimit, then routers; each route file exports a function(Router) that registers its own path+middleware, and Router.ts calls them (order matters for overlapping paths).

topic: how auth works for users, bots, OAuth2, webhooks and sockets (token to cached user)
hint: authenticate() reads raw Authorization header, authenticateUser decrypts token to a session id, loads user from redis cache, also checks IP bans and updates allowed-IP cache; bots rejected unless allowBot. Webhook tokens use JWT_WEBHOOK_SECRET and are matched to webhook id.

topic: how server/channel permissions are enforced (role bits, channel overrides, owner/admin bypass, member cache)
hint: Chain populates req.serverCache/serverMemberCache/channelCache; owner (serverCache.createdById) and ROLE_PERMISSIONS.ADMIN short-circuit both role and channel checks; member permissions are an OR of role bits cached in a redis hash.

topic: how to add a new REST endpoint (route file, Router registration, middleware, validation, service, emit)
hint: Handlers return [result,error] tuples (CustomResult) and errors via generateError; validation uses express-validator then customExpressValidatorResult.

topic: how rate limiting works (global limit, per-route, redis cache, in dev mode)
hint: rateLimit is skipped entirely in DEV_MODE unless body.test_enable_rate_limit is set; key is userId (or IP fallback) plus name; nextIfRatedLimited lets handlers continue with req.rateLimited.

topic: how a message is created and delivered (route, validation, DB write, mentions, socket emit, push notification)
hint: Message.ts exports createMessage = createMessageV2 from MessageCreate.ts; webhooks also reach createMessage.

topic: how realtime events flow: socket connect/authenticate, rooms, emit helpers, multi-process delivery
hint: Socket.io uses the redis-streams adapter so the api process emits to sockets held by the ws process; emitToAll broadcasts to rooms keyed by serverIds, friendIds and userId, and an empty room array would broadcast to everyone; sockets get 30s to emit AUTHENTICATE; auth is serialized through a concurrency-1 PQueue.

topic: server lifecycle: create/join/leave/ban/delete (scheduled deletion), and the caches that must be kept in sync
hint: Servers are soft-deleted via scheduledForDeletion and removed by scheduleServerDeletion in src/index.ts; verification middleware rejects scheduled-for-deletion servers unless ignoreScheduledDeletion.

topic: moderation and admin: mod badges, suspensions, IP bans, audit logs
hint: isModMiddleware gates on USER_BADGES FOUNDER/ADMIN (MOD only when allowModBadge) badge bits on req.userCache.badges.

topic: user account lifecycle: register/login, sessions/devices, account deletion and background cleanup jobs
hint: deleteAccount and the schedule*Deletion jobs in src/index.ts remove content in 300-item batches via setInterval.

topic: Redis cache layer and key conventions (user, presence, server, channel caches; flush on boot)
hint: customRedisFlush runs in the primary process at boot (src/index.ts); worker exit kills all clusters to avoid stale socket.io online-user data.
